gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TESSAN's long flat-cord strips (PS07 with 5/10/15 ft cords, PS09 with 10 ft) top out at 1,250 W, while CRST's metal strips with 15 ft 14 AWG cords are rated 15 A / 1,875 W for $24.99–$49.99 on crsttech.com.
standout_why: I compared against three pages. rottenwifi.com gives cord gauge (14 AWG) and 15 A only for the 10 ft Belkin BE112234-10 and the 6 ft TLP606B, and covers no strip with a 15 ft or longer cord. ChatGPT's cards for the TESSAN 15 ft and 25 ft strips list cord length, outlets and USB but no watt rating or gauge. The CRST pages in its results give CRST's own 14 AWG / 1,875 W figures but never compare them with TESSAN. I could not load gearlark.com (certificate error), so it is not in this comparison.
decides: It tilts the pick for anyone powering more than phones and lamps at the end of a long run. A 1,250 W cap at 120 V is about 10.4 A. CRST's 15 ft 14 AWG strips are rated for the full 15 A / 1,875 W at a similar or lower price. Our TESSAN PS07 has a 15 ft cord option and 2,100 J, so it fits a long-cord light-load list but loses on load capacity.
